title: Concept: Network error text discloses an internal address and port
description: A rendered connection error that names the private address and port it failed to reach tells the caller how the internal network is numbered and which service sits where. It is the one form of internal disclosure an unauthenticated caller can induce at will, because they only have to break a request.
applicability: Responses from an application that sits behind a private network and renders error or diagnostic text.
risk: The caller learns the internal addressing and the port of a backend service, and can usually induce the same error repeatedly, so the internal map can be built request by request.
